steps.title: Check the source
steps.body: Look at who posted the content first. Is it a verified account, a known news outlet, or an anonymous page? Unverified or brand-new accounts are a red flag.

steps.title: Reverse image search
steps.body: Search the image on Google Images or TinEye to see where else it has appeared. If it shows up in unrelated stories or much older posts, treat it with suspicion.

steps.title: Verify the date
steps.body: Old photos and videos are often recirculated out of context to look like breaking news. Check when the content was first published before reacting to it.

steps.title: Cross-check with trusted sources
steps.body: See if established, reputable outlets are reporting the same thing. If only one obscure source has the story, wait for confirmation before trusting it.

steps.title: Decide whether to share
steps.body: If you're still unsure after checking the source, searching the image, and verifying the date, don't share it. When in doubt, sit it out.

pause.title: Pause.
pause.lede: Three quick checks before this leaves your hands.
pause.check3Label: Does it make you feel a strong emotion?
pause.cooldownNote: Take a breath — sharing unlocks in a moment
pause.practiceNote: Practice mode — scan an image first to actually share it.

deepfakeHelp.intro: Here's what to do in the first few minutes.
deepfakeHelp.reassurance: Work through these in order. You don't have to do all of them at once.

steps.title: Stop
steps.body: Don't share, forward, or screenshot it further. Even sharing it to warn others can spread the harm and make it harder to get removed.

steps.title: Save evidence
steps.body: Take a screenshot and save the link or URL before it disappears. You'll need this if you report it or ask an adult for help.

steps.title: Report it
steps.body: Report the content directly to the platform it's on — most platforms remove non-consensual or deepfake content quickly once reported.

steps.title: Tell someone you trust
steps.body: A parent, teacher, school counselor, or other trusted adult can help you take the next steps. You don't have to handle this alone.

steps.title: It is not your fault
steps.body: Being targeted by a deepfake is not something you caused. The responsibility is entirely on the person who made or shared it.
